name: YugabyteDB
model: Tables of rows with SQL via YSQL, which reuses PostgreSQL's query layer (high Postgres compatibility); also YCQL, a Cassandra-style API
engine_note: DocDB: a document store built on a modified RocksDB (LSM); tables split into tablets, each replicated by Raft
consistency: Multi-row, cross-node transactions. Levels: serializable, snapshot, read committed; read committed is default for v2025.2+ via yugabyted, Anywhere or Aeon, else snapshot. Writes commit through Raft majorities; follower and read-replica reads are opt-in and can be stale.

jepsen.finding: Found two read skew bugs (one in healthy clusters, one under clock skew) and occasional loss of inserted rows during partitions; fixed in 1.2.0 except a minor availability issue.
Serializable SQL transactions showed G2-item (anti-dependency) cycles, fixed in 1.3.1.2-b1; DEFAULT column initialisation and some DDL issues were left open.

scaling: Automatic sharding (hash or range) into tablets that split and rebalance as you add nodes; read replicas and multi-region placements.
licence: Apache License 2.0 (core database); YugabyteDB Anywhere management platform under Polyform Free Trial 1.0.0

licence_events.event: All formerly enterprise database features moved to Apache 2.0 (one fully open-source edition); the management platform put under the Polyform Free Trial licence.

version_note: Stable series are named by year; 2026.1 is the newest series on GitHub releases.
reach: Reach for it when you want to keep Postgres SQL and drivers but need writes spread over many nodes or regions with automatic failover.
avoid: Avoid when one Postgres server is enough (higher latency per query, more nodes to run), or you rely on Postgres extensions it does not support.
escape: You leave the Postgres default for this because writes outgrow one machine but you want to keep Postgres SQL.
chat: Users, chats and messages for a global product that wants Postgres compatibility with multi-region writes.
notes: Isolation defaults quoted from the isolation-levels page on 2026-10-04 (read committed default only for v2025.2+ deployments through yugabyted, Anywhere or Aeon; manual deployments fall back to snapshot). Licence from LICENSE.md on master. Jepsen 2019 reports noted YugabyteDB depends on clock synchronisation.
